notes: An open alternative exists: Hanks's University of Maryland MS thesis on the same experiments (2009, DRUM hdl 1903/9105), fetched to docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/Hanks_2009_thesis.pdf. Its abstract (PDF p. 1) says, in hypoxia (< 40 % saturation), "metabolic rates increased as much as 4-fold while growth decreased 3-fold"; the treatments were 20, 40 and ≥ 70 % saturation at 6–28 °C, and its Figs. 17–18 give energy densities. None of this confirms the article's own numbers (thesis values can differ from the paper), so the claims stay unchecked; the rewrite could cite the thesis instead, after a reader checks it. The human can open the article through a library via the DOI.
